title: Load test harness for burst pools + neighbor tail-latency regression checks
author: Peter Holtz
description: Summary: Adds a GPU-backed load test harness (burstbench) that exercises Dedicated baseline + burst behavior with a paired “neighbor” tenant and fails the run when neighbor tail latency regresses beyond configured thresholds. The harness produces a structured report (JSON) and JUnit output for CI consumption, and optionally uploads run artifacts (latency histograms + admission/denial breakdown) to GCS for SRE review. Motivation: During burst beta we had a couple near-misses where burst admission was “correct” but non-burst neighbors saw measurable p99 tail amplification under certain batching/telemetry conditions. We need an automated, repeatable test that detects noisy-neighbor regressions before GA tuning/rollouts. This PR implements the core scenarios + an analyzer/gate that can be used in nightly and pre-GA release qualification runs. What’s included: (1) New tool `tools/burstbench/` (Go) that can generate two-tenant traffic against a staging or perf cluster using Redwood gateway APIs, with deterministic request shapes and seeded randomness. (2) Scenario library for `baseline_only`, `burst_window`, and `burst_with_cooldown` with knobs for request rate ramps, max concurrency, streaming/non-streaming mix, and token distributions. (3) Analyzer that computes p50/p95/p99 per tenant, plus “neighbor delta” metrics: `neighbor_p95_delta_ms`, `neighbor_p99_delta_ms`, and `tail_amplification_ratio` (p99/p50) before vs during burst window. (4) Regression gate config (`tools/burstbench/configs/guardrails.yaml`) with defaults aligned to Dedicated non-burst SLO protection: fail run if neighbor p95 increases by > 40ms or neighbor p99 increases by > 120ms for >= 3 consecutive 1m buckets; warn-only thresholds are also emitted. (5) Buildkite step + documentation for running in nightly on `perf-us-east-h100` (gated behind a flag; does not run on every PR by default due to GPU cost). (6) Prometheus query snapshots embedded in the report (best-effort) to correlate admission controller denials/queueing and router fallback events during the test window. Notes/assumptions: - This uses real staging/perf infra with Dedicated + burst pool enabled; it does not attempt to fully emulate kernel-level contention in unit tests. The only “fast” CI coverage is the analyzer unit tests + report formatting. - Tenant IDs are passed explicitly; we do not create tenants as part of the test (avoids control-plane flakiness). - The harness labels are constrained to avoid high cardinality in metrics; per Allison’s guidance, we only tag `scenario`, `run_id`, `region`, and `hardware_class` (no tenant names in metrics). How to run: `bazel run //tools/burstbench:burstbench -- --config tools/burstbench/configs/burst_window_us_east_h100.yaml --run_id local-<ts> --target https://gateway.perf.us-east.redwood.ai` (see README for required auth + allowlist). Outputs: - `artifacts/report.json` (full run) - `artifacts/junit.xml` (gating) - `artifacts/summary.txt` (human readable) - Optional upload to `gs://redwood-perf-artifacts/burstbench/<run_id>/` when `--upload_artifacts` is set. Rollout: Start with nightly + manual pre-release qualification. Once stable (2 weeks) we can consider enabling the analyzer gate on release branches for burst-related changes only (label-driven).
commits: burstbench scenarios: baseline + burst window + cooldown
analyzer: neighbor delta + tail amplification calculations
reporting: JSON + JUnit output, artifact bundling
review_conversation: Sean Gallagher (review): Can we make the failure criteria explicit in the PR description and ensure they map to “non-burst protection” rather than “burst customer success”? I want to avoid a test that silently incentivizes loosening guardrails. Also: please add a note about bucket duration and consecutive-bucket logic (we’ve been bitten by flappy gates). Peter Holtz (author): Updated README + PR description; guardrails are explicitly neighbor-protection oriented. Added `--bucket_duration` and documented default 60s with a 3-bucket consecutive requirement to fail. Allison Grant (review): Please do not emit tenant IDs/names as metric labels. Also, make sure the report includes the exact query window boundaries so we can correlate in Grafana. Peter Holtz (author): Removed tenant label entirely; metrics now only include scenario/run_id/region/hwclass. Added report fields `window_start_rfc3339` and `window_end_rfc3339` plus per-phase boundaries. Keiko Yamamoto (review): The p95/p99 delta thresholds look plausible, but can we make them config-only (no constants) and add a warn band? Also, does cooldown scenario verify that denials drop after cooldown? Peter Holtz (author): Thresholds moved to `guardrails.yaml`, and analyzer emits WARN vs FAIL states. Cooldown scenario now asserts that `BURST_COOLDOWN_ACTIVE` denials dominate for the configured cooldown duration and then decrease once cooldown expires (reported as a check, not a gate yet). Mina Haddad (review): For the router correlation, do we rely on log scraping or Prometheus? Prefer Prometheus queries. Also ensure we record fallback rate (baseline vs burst admitted). Peter Holtz (author): Switched to Prometheus query snapshotting via the internal query API (best-effort, non-fatal). Added fallback counters to the report: `router_fallback_rate` and `admission_denial_rate` for the burst window. Ravi Menon (review): Minor: rename “neighbor” to “non_burst_neighbor” in the report to make semantics clear. Also, can we add a scenario knob for streaming vs non-streaming? Peter Holtz (author): Renamed fields and added `streaming_mix` to scenario config. Final approvals: Sean Gallagher (approved), Allison Grant (approved), Keiko Yamamoto (approved), Mina Haddad (approved).
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main after approvals; nightly perf step enabled behind `PERF_NIGHTLY_BURSTBENCH=1` on the perf pipeline only.
release_notes: Internal: Added burstbench load test harness + neighbor latency regression gate (nightly/perf only). No customer-facing changes.
